verdict.line: You lose if you let him stack Siphoning Strike uncontested into his level 6 Fury of the Sands; you win if you deny his farm and force all-ins before he gets there.

brief.thesis: Nasus's entire scaling plan depends on landing Siphoning Strike (255 range) repeatedly and safely, and Cho'Gath has the tools to make that unsafe: Rupture reaches out to 950 range to engage or punish his last-hits, and Feral Scream is a 300-range cone silence that shuts down his Wither counter-engage mid-trade. Nasus has no real pressure tool until Fury of the Sands comes online at level 6, so the lane is structurally yours before that point and risky for you only in the window right after.

theirWindow.when: At level 6 with Fury of the Sands up
theirWindow.what: Fury of the Sands grants him extra health, range, and a nearby max-health drain for its duration — do not stand in prolonged melee range once he pops it, disengage and reset instead of trading blow for blow.

yourWindow.what: Open with Rupture for the knockup and slow, follow immediately with Feral Scream to silence him out of Wither, then auto-attack to stack Vorpal Spikes; he has no tool at this stage that beats that combo.

start.why: Run by 80.8% of Cho'Gaths in this matchup at a 50.8% win rate — the extra sustain and mana keep your Rupture/Feral Scream combo spammable through the early all-in window.

boots.why: Higher measured win rate than Plated Steelcaps (54.8% vs 50.5%) — the movement speed lets you reset after an all-in or close distance when he tries to kite with Wither.

core.why: The highest-win-rate core path recorded (66.7% over 12 games) — stacks health that makes your point-blank Rupture engages safer.
Punishes his lifesteal-heavy Soul Eater passive and the attack speed he gets from stacked Siphoning Strike kills.
Caps the top win-rate build path and adds sustained AoE pressure for extended trades.

runes.keystoneWhy: The burst attack speed window fits the all-in trade pattern this matchup rewards — it front-loads Vorpal Spikes procs exactly when you're forcing a fight before level 6.

summoners.why: The most-played and best-performing combo (50.8% win rate, 62.4% pick) — Teleport lets you reset waves after all-ins and keep pace with his split-push if the lane goes long; Flash+Ignite is viable if you want to force pre-6 kills but trails in measured win rate (46.4%).

playing.title: Punish his CS stacking
playing.detail: Every time he goes to land Siphoning Strike on a minion, step up and contest with Rupture — a Nasus denied clean stacks scales dramatically slower.

playing.title: All-in before level 6
playing.detail: Combo Q into W into autos while he only has a single-target Q (255 range) and Wither; neither stops your burst.

playing.title: Silence through his Wither
playing.detail: Land Feral Scream's silence before he can cast Wither on you mid-trade so your Vorpal Spikes keep landing clean without the attack-speed penalty.

playing.title: Respect the level 6 spike
playing.detail: Once Fury of the Sands is up, back off extended fights — its health drain and range buff flip trades fast.

playing.title: Save Feast for the kill
playing.detail: Feast's true damage (60s cooldown) is your best execute; securing the kill grows your max HP (up to 6 stacks) and compounds your lead.

playing.title: Track his stack count all game
playing.detail: A Nasus kept near zero kills by 10 minutes is close to useless in a 1v1 — keep interrupting any farm attempt you can reach.

playing.title: Avoid late 1v1s at full build
playing.detail: With infinite Q stacking and Fury of the Sands online, extended late-game duels favor him — end fights fast or disengage rather than standing in prolonged trades.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, boots, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/sample figures above are measured OP.GG data from live games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and trade timing are my own read of the kit interactions.

stats.opponentTip: Do not let Nasus farm during early game by fighting him often. Avoid being killed when he reaches level 6 and uses Unbound Spellbook – (R).
